subject.title: [Feature]: [Feature Request] 按用户维度统计 Token 使用量

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-user token usage accounting in core, and which principal should define a user for usage attribution?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary changes identity, privacy, storage, Gateway RPC, Dashboard, and quota/billing semantics in a project documented around a trusted single-operator gateway model.

options.title: Core Identity Accounting
options.body: Define the user principal, authorized readers, storage schema, aggregation RPCs, Dashboard and `/usage` behavior, retention, and redaction rules before implementation.

options.title: External Reporting First
options.body: Keep core usage as session, agent, channel, model, and provider aggregates while Pinchy-style front layers or plugins build user billing reports from explicit identity mappings.

options.title: Keep Single-Operator Scope
options.body: Decline core multi-user accounting for now and limit future work to existing session, agent, and provider usage improvements.

recommendation.title: Core Identity Accounting
recommendation.body: Define the user principal, authorized readers, storage schema, aggregation RPCs, Dashboard and `/usage` behavior, retention, and redaction rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest usage/cost surface history and can route the identity/security half to Gateway auth owners.
